title: epic: Research cockpit — dockview docking shell (replaces top-nav)
body:
Exploration. Evaluate https://dockview.dev (MIT, local, no network) as a docking/split-pane layout framework, piloted on the Companies/Spolki workspace. Motivation: the report-diff presentation problem (master-detail / side-by-side reading of section diffs) and the narrow-window constraints we fought are exactly what a docking framework addresses with resizable, dockable panes. Scope: a contained pilot on one view; measure ergonomics, bundle size, a11y, theming fit with the night-neon identity, and narrow-window behavior. 
Decision gates: it is a new runtime UI dependency, so adoption requires a new ADR extending ADR 0037 (UI component framework). Keep it primitive-first inside panes. Do NOT broaden beyond the pilot without the ADR. If adopted, the report-diff presentation v2 likely lands inside a dockview pane.

comments.body:
Pivot (ADR 0053 rewritten): the inline-workspace pilot was rejected as a HOST (nested scroll, fixed height, div-tab a11y) — but the real opportunity is bigger. Decision: adopt dockview as the app-wide research-cockpit shell (full canvas replacing the ADR-0047 single-screen top-nav), not one view. Maintainer chose FULL cockpit over hybrid.

Spike landed (green, make check-frontend: 316 tests/lint/stylelint/knip/build): full-screen Cockpit screen (src/screens/Cockpit/), reachable via a new 'Cockpit' nav entry, with accessible tabs (axe-clean, in the screens.a11y guard), cross-company side-by-side default layout, open-panel toolbar, and best-effort localStorage layout persistence. Reused: --dv-* token bridge, DockLayout adapter, ESLint containment guardrail (now scoped to src/screens/Cockpit/), ResizeObserver test polyfill.

This is now an EPIC. Open decisions needing sign-off (see ADR 0053 'Open decisions'): (1) migration path off ADR 0047; (2) saved/named layouts = settings/data-model contract + migration + dockview-JSON versioning; (3) command palette as panel launcher (v0.48.0); (4) per-panel data wiring beyond companyId-only panels; (5) full keyboard model; (6) pop-out windows (ultrawide/FancyZones); (7) default layouts + reset. Screenshots of the working cockpit captured under tests/browser/__cockpit-evidence__/.

title: Frontend: dodać ESLint layering gate (granice warstw ui/shared/app/api); workspaces i path-aliases odrzucone
body:
## Decyzja (podjęta w analizie 2026-06-22)

Pytanie: czy modularyzować frontend pod npm/Node workspaces, i/lub wprowadzić tsconfig path aliases + ESLint layering gate.

**Rozstrzygnięte — NIE zaczynaj od nowa:**

1. **npm/Node workspaces — ODRZUCONE.** Repo ma jeden `package.json` (brak `workspaces`), jeden `package-lock.json`, brak pnpm/yarn/lerna/nx/turbo. Frontend ma jednego konsumenta (aplikacja Tauri), jeden build (`tsc && vite build`), jeden deploy. Workspaces rozwiązują problem linkowania wielu pakietów/konsumentów — tego problemu nie ma. Dodatkowo kłóciłyby się z release tooling, który robi *zsynchronizowany single version bump* (package.json + Cargo.toml + tauri.conf.json + asercja w lib.rs, gate `release:version-check`) — wiele package.json = nowa powierzchnia na rozjazd. Sprzeczne z AGENTS.md ("avoid premature complexity not tied to a real planned extension").

2. **tsconfig/vite path aliases (`@ui`, `@shared`…) — ODŁOŻONE (nie warto teraz).** Istnieje 311 importów `../../…`, ale: alias trzeba synchronizować w 3–4 configach (tsconfig/vite/vitest/Playwright); istniejąca reguła `no-restricted-imports` w `eslint.config.js` *dosłownie* instruuje wzorzec `from "../../ui"`, więc alias = przepisanie reguły + churn 311 miejsc (prawie każdy ekran, ogromny diff, zaśmiecony git blame); zysk czysto estetyczny; brak drugiego konsumenta = brak korzyści z przenośności. Relatywne importy nie są zepsute. Wrócić do tematu DOPIERO gdy pojawi się drugi konsument UI (osobny web build, Storybook, publikowany `@brawler/ui`) — wtedy aliasy + workspaces wracają razem.

3. **ESLint layering gate — REKOMENDOWANE DO ZROBIENIA.** To właściwa ścieżka realizacji celu "modularność / egzekwowane granice".

## Co zrobić (slice do implementacji)

Rozszerzyć istniejącą regułę `no-restricted-imports` w `eslint.config.js` (ta sama reguła, która już pilnuje barrela `src/ui`) o wzorce warstwowe, które zamrażają dziś-prawdziwe granice jako twardy gate w `make check`. Pasuje do enforcement-as-guardrails (ADR 0038).

**Stan faktyczny (zweryfikowany w analizie):**
- Warstwy: `src/ui` (34 pliki, **czysty liść** — nie importuje screens/app/api), `src/shared` (36), `src/app` (36), `src/api` (240), `src/screens` (73).
- `src/ui` ma barrel `index.ts`; istnieje już guardrail "importuj prymitywy z barrela, nie z deep path".

**Pierwsza, bezpieczna reguła:** `ui ↛ screens|app|api` (zweryfikowane jako dziś czyste — zero naruszeń).

**KRYTYCZNE zastrzeżenie (reguła guardrail-harvest, ADR 0045):** nigdy nie dodawaj szerokiej bramki, która flaguje legalny kod. Każdą kolejną proponowaną granicę (`shared ↛ screens`, `screens ↛ screens`, itp.) NAJPIERW przeskanuj pod kątem istniejących naruszeń. Jeśli istnieją legalne naruszenia → pomiń tę regułę albo najpierw posprzątaj kod, nie wpuszczaj hałaśliwej bramki. Zacznij od `ui-leaf`, rozszerzaj ostrożnie.

**Zakres slice'a:** zmiana w `eslint.config.js` + krótka notka w `docs/modularization-design.md` (i ew. odwołanie przy ADR 0038), zgodnie z wymogiem guardrail-harvest by guardrail trafił do kanonicznego doca. Bez nowej zależności, bez churn-u importów.

## Pliki referencyjne
- `eslint.config.js:107` — istniejąca reguła `no-restricted-imports` (barrel ui)
- `eslint.config.js` `no-restricted-syntax` / `PRIMITIVE_FIRST` — istniejący primitive-first gate
- `src/ui/index.ts` — barrel
- `docs/adr/0038-enforcement-as-guardrails.md`, `docs/adr/0045-guardrail-harvest-loop.md`, `docs/modularization-design.md`

title: Enforce nix-only Rust validation to eliminate host/nix toolchain skew
body: The host sandbox toolchain is split — cargo/rustc 1.96 (~/.local/bin) but rustdoc 1.95 (nix) — which produced false cargo-test --doc failures (E0514) and hid a real clippy lint (collapsible_match, 1.95-only) during v0.44.0. 'Green' on the host did not mean green under nix. Fix options: (a) standardize all Rust build/test/lint validation on nix (make targets / nix develop -c) and document that host-toolchain results don't count; (b) align the host toolchain to the nix-pinned version. Prefer (a) as robust-by-construction. Add a rule to engineering-workflow.md. title: Migrate AI provider/job layer from blocking to async
body:
Foundation for the multi-provider AI milestone: convert the analysis provider boundary and its jobs from reqwest::blocking to async, so all downstream provider work (registry, Claude, OpenAI, document input) is async-first and ready to swap the in-house provider lib for official Anthropic/OpenAI Rust SDKs when they exist.

Rationale:
- Tauri already runs on tokio; reqwest::blocking wraps async reqwest, so blocking pays the async cost without the benefits.
- Future official SDKs (and all current community crates) are async-first; going async now makes the later in-house->SDK swap a drop-in rather than a prerequisite refactor.
- Enables concurrency for the autonomous report pipeline (v0.47) and streaming responses (AI waiting animation).

Scope:
- Make AiAnalysisProvider an async trait (async-trait for boxed dyn dispatch); add the async-trait dependency.
- Migrate the Gemini analysis adapter and its injectable HTTP client trait to async (reqwest async).
- Migrate the three analysis jobs (ai_analysis, research_briefs, research_digests) and the Tauri commands that invoke them to async.
- Migrate the transcription provider and transcript_runner to async as well (stays Gemini-only; async for consistency).
- Tests move to #[tokio::test] with a mockable async transport seam; CI stays offline (no live provider calls).

Out of scope:
- Adding Claude/OpenAI providers (later tasks); the registry/port refactor (its own task); any official SDK adoption.

Exit criteria:
- The provider boundary and all AI jobs/commands compile and run async; Gemini analysis and transcription behavior is unchanged.
- Deterministic async tests pass with no live external calls; clippy -D warnings and fmt clean.

title: test harness: reuseExistingServer can serve a stale build to the browser suite (false-green visual/density baselines)
body: Observed 2026-07-09 during Panel B QG: a long-lived Playwright webServer (reuseExistingServer: true) kept serving pre-rework code — the report-documents M-dark visual shot byte-matched a baseline from BEFORE the panel rework across multiple runs (incl. --update-snapshots, which respects the diff threshold and so kept the stale file), while a fresh server rendered the new layout. Consequence: an agent can generate/verify baselines against stale code and report green. Fix ideas: (a) make the browser-suite entry (make ui-smoke / check) assert the served bundle's freshness (e.g. inject a build hash endpoint and compare against the working tree), (b) reuseExistingServer: false for baseline-updating runs, or (c) a pre-suite guard that kills servers older than the newest src mtime. Class: false-green gate — priority high per ADR 0038 spirit.

comments.body: Fixed (option a — served-bundle freshness assert). The config computes a build stamp = newest mtime across src/ at eval time, bakes it into the webServer it starts (VITE_BRAWLER_BUILD_STAMP -> window.__BRAWLER_BUILD_STAMP__, smoke-only), and records it as BRAWLER_EXPECTED_BUILD_STAMP. A new tests/browser/global-setup.ts runs after the server is up and before any spec: it reads the stamp the RUNNING server actually baked and aborts the whole suite on a mismatch. A reused stale dev server (another worktree/branch, or from before the latest edit) carries a different baked stamp -> loud abort instead of a false-green baseline; a freshly-started server bakes the same value -> passes, so the normal make ui-smoke flow (no pre-existing server) is unaffected. No CI dependency. Verified end-to-end against a real vite smoke build: served===expected -> guard allows; served!==expected -> guard aborts. docs/testing.md gained one line documenting the guard + the fix (stop the stale server on :4321).

title: Atrem cash facts differ by ~1000x between years — suspected unit-scale defect
body: Found during v0.59 orchestrator verification (2026-07-21) while checking whether the period-derivation 'roczn' bug had corrupted stored data (it had not — see below). Concrete case, owner's live DB, company_gpw_atr, kpidef_cash: FY2023=19000, Q1-2024=17000, FY2024=17000, then Q1-2025=3841000, Q3-2025=2315000, FY2025=8529000 (the last from the esef tier, the earlier ones from pdf). A three-orders-of-magnitude jump across the tier boundary strongly suggests the earlier pdf-tier values were recorded WITHOUT the 'w tys.' multiplier — i.e. 17000 should be 17,000,000. Systemic check: of 63 consecutive-FY value pairs in the DB, exactly 1 shows a >100x jump, so this is currently ISOLATED, not widespread — but a silent 1000x error in a financial fact is severe (it flows into ratios, health scores, and any valuation work), and the unit multiplier is exactly the kind of thing that fails per-company-template rather than globally. Scope: confirm against the source filings, find whether the pdf tier's unit handling or the specific extraction profile is at fault, add a reddening test from this exact document, and decide on repair (forward migration or re-extraction) for affected rows. Note: this was NOT caused by, and is unrelated to, the period-derivation fix in the same milestone.

body:
Odkrycie z live-drive'u F5 (2026-07-10, realna baza, sweep CDR: 10 runów, limit 2, AI 0/2):

1. 9/10 kandydatów CDR to XHTML-e raportów ŚRÓDROCZNYCH bez tagowania iXBRL (mandat ESEF obejmuje tylko raporty roczne — settled regulation). parse_esef nie wyprowadza okresu -> derive_report_period zwraca None -> delta not_extractable. Jedyny sukces: paczka .xbri FY2025 (12 faktów, tier esef, deterministycznie).
2. Tier-4 (OCR) jest PDF-only, a kanoniczny slot tych okresów trzyma XHTML — więc tier-4 nie ma wejścia, mimo że dla części tych samych okresów w bazie leżą równoległe, niekanoniczne PDF-y (nigdy nie próbowane).

Kierunki (do decyzji, opcje z tradeoffami przy planowaniu):
a) fallback okresu z tytułu/URL dla XHTML, gdy iXBRL nie parsuje (odblokowuje sam okres, nie ekstrakcję),
b) sweep próbuje najlepszy EKSTRAKTOWALNY dokument okresu (siostrzany PDF), nie ślepo kanoniczny,
c) deterministyczny parser tabel XHTML (śródroczne XHTML to zwykły HTML z tabelami — pokrewny torowi bankier/tier-2, potencjalnie DUŻO tańszy niż OCR).

Powiązane: mis-asocjacje 45fcece (jedyni PDF-owi kandydaci CBF to dokumenty Energi/Vercomu z terminalnymi runami).

title: epic: Quality frameworks — quantitative checks
body:
Goal: evaluate a company against user-owned quality checklists using deterministic rules over the fundamentals facts, producing a versioned scorecard. Ship clonable templates including a Kroeze-style quality framework.

A framework is a named, user-owned set of criteria (your Kroeze checklist is one; other investors define their own). This epic covers the quantitative half: criteria that are testable against the facts/derived metrics with no AI (e.g. roic >= 15%, net_debt_to_ebitda < 2.5, fcf > 0, revenue CAGR > 10%). A rule engine evaluates them exactly and records measured values.

Depends on: fundamentals facts (v0.36). Independent of v0.43-v0.46, so it can be resequenced earlier or later.

Scope:
- frameworks data model and ADR (frameworks, criteria, evaluations, criterion results; rule expression grammar over KPI keys and thresholds; user-owned plus app-template origin)
- storage, commands, DTOs
- deterministic rule engine over facts and derived metrics, producing per-criterion pass/partial/fail with measured value
- seed app templates including a Kroeze-style quality framework, clonable and editable
- frameworks UI: manage frameworks/criteria, run evaluation, scorecard per company with verdicts, measured values, and history
- export/import of frameworks and evaluations

Out of scope: qualitative/agent-assessed criteria (next epic); any buy/sell scoring (decision support only).

Exit criteria: a user can clone the Kroeze template, evaluate a real company (e.g. cyber_Folks) against its quantitative criteria, and see a scorecard with measured values that updates as new facts arrive.

body:
Research whether https://pl.investing.com/webmaster-tools/rss can be a reliable and acceptable source for Brawler.

Questions to answer:
- What RSS feeds are available and which markets/company scopes do they cover?
- Are terms of use and webmaster-tool conditions compatible with Brawler's public/open-core app distribution?

epic: Test architecture v2 — data-transform correctness at volume
body:
Successor to the test-architecture foundation epic (5eabef7, ADR 0048). Non-product, cross-cutting test-infra epic (no milestone:vX.Y.0); lands ahead of v0.46 so the harness exists before the data-heavy epics it guards (story clustering v0.46, autonomous report pipeline v0.49, report-over-report diff v0.47, cross-company KPI comparison v0.53).

Brawler's correctness risk is shifting from CRUD to DATA TRANSFORMS — dedup, normalization, entity matching/reconciliation, merge — which fail on the long tail and at volume, not the happy path. A QA review found the matching gaps: property-based testing essentially absent (1 proptest!), no golden snapshots (insta), no perf/scale tests (the v0.45.0 find_similar UI-freeze class), no parser fuzzing, unverified mock-runtime fidelity (ts-rs guarantees shapes not behavior), no end-to-end ingestion pipeline test, narrow mutation scope.

Design: ADR 0049 (extends ADR 0048). Decisions: (1) property/invariant testing as a first-class layer; (2) golden insta snapshots for parser/normalization output; (3) parser fuzzing via proptest/arbitrary on the STABLE toolchain (cargo-fuzz rejected — needs nightly, splits the Nix toolchain); (4) behavioral+deterministic scale gates in make check + periodic criterion benches with a relative ratchet (never wall-clock hard gate); (5) dual-execution mock-fidelity contract (TS mock runtime vs real Rust AppState/storage layer); (6) e2e ingestion pipeline tests (adapter->storage->read-model); (7) mutation scope follows the transform surface.

New dev-deps (none ship): insta, criterion, arbitrary (proptest already present). Implemented big-bang against today's transforms; v0.46+ epics extend the same harness.

Child tasks linked via parent:<this-hex7>:
T1 property-based transform layer · T2 golden snapshots + fixtures->samples · T3 parser fuzzing · T4 scale behavioral gates · T5 periodic criterion benches + ratchet · T6 dual-execution mock-fidelity contract · T7 e2e ingestion pipeline test · T8 mutation-scope expansion.

title: epic: Architecture v2 — domain stores, source pipeline, entity resolution, durable jobs, frontend decomposition, vector scaling
body:
Foundational, cross-cutting epic (no milestone:vX.Y.0; lands ahead of v0.46.0), the structural counterpart to the test-architecture work (epics 5eabef7 / 3c0bce0) and made safe to attempt BY it — every child is a behavior-preserving refactor guarded by the ADR 0049 harness (dual-execution mock-fidelity contract, golden snapshots, transform invariants, e2e pipeline test). Harden tests first, then refactor, is the deliberate sequence.

Design: ADR 0050 (extends/realizes ADR 0039 ports posture, ADR 0035 interpretation port, ADR 0032 storage boundaries). Six children, each sequenced ahead of the feature it unblocks:

1. Split the 207-method AppState facade into concrete DOMAIN STORES (CompanyStore/FeedStore/...). NOT a repository port — ADR 0039's storage non-port stance stands; concrete SQLite-coupled structs, strangler migration. Foundational/early.
2. Realize the SourceAdapter PORT: a trait + registry (the port architecture.md/ADR 0039 already declare but code does not implement). Strangler-migrate the 8 adapters. Before v0.46.
3. One generic INGESTION PIPELINE (parse->normalize->resolve-entity->dedup->upsert->derive) + an ENTITY-RESOLUTION module (canonical company id + canonical story key). The v0.46 clustering / v0.53 compare enabler. Depends on #2. Plugs into the ADR 0049 invariant harness.
4. FRONTEND STATE DECOMPOSITION: break AppStateRoot (~1967 lines, ~146 hooks) + god-hooks into feature-scoped state. Before v0.48 (triage + command palette). Stays primitive-first (ADR 0037).
5. Durable SQLite-backed JOB QUEUE (jobs table + worker loop, claim/retry/resume) + Rust-side scheduler, replacing fire-and-forget spawn_blocking. Before v0.49 (autonomous pipeline). Local-first; no heavy new dep.
6. ANN VECTOR-INDEX swap behind the interpretation port (ADR 0035), near v0.53; T4 scale gate guards the contract. Scheduled, not immediate.

Children linked via parent:<this-hex7>.

title: Backfill automated test coverage for behaviors shipped before the full-coverage policy
body:
The testing policy changed (AGENTS.md Testing Expectations + docs/testing.md): aim for automated coverage of EVERY behavior — every command/contract, read model, UI workflow, migration, source adapter, provider mapping, job, and fixed regression has a test that fails when it breaks. Behaviors shipped before this change likely lack tests; this task closes that backfill gap.

Scope:
- Audit the codebase for untested behaviors across the layers (Rust unit/contract, Vitest component/workflow, sample-backed integration). Start from the command surface (src-tauri commands), read models, migrations, adapters, jobs, and UI workflows.
- Backfill tests in the CHEAPEST layer that proves each behavior. Behavior/contract assertions, not implementation details.
- Keep it lean and fast: no redundant/brittle/screenshot tests; one good test per behavior; the slow/credentialed layers (Playwright/live/packaging smoke) stay opt-in/periodic so make check does not balloon. Watch make check wall-time as coverage grows.

Approach: incremental and prioritized (high-risk/high-value areas first — storage/migrations, command contracts, AI mapping, source adapters). May be promoted to an epic and split into per-area tasks if it proves large. Not a blocker for current milestone work; going forward the Definition of Done already requires a test for each new behavior, so this is strictly about pre-policy debt.

title: Testing: type the mock-runtime handler returns against the generated IPC contract
body:
Follow-up from the mock-layer unification (749a5a8, ADR 0048). The unified mock runtime (`src/test/scenarios/runtime.ts`) hand-implements all 156 IPC command handlers; each returns `unknown`. The completeness guardrail covers read non-emptiness and the broad clickable suites exercise most commands, but a handler can still return the wrong SHAPE for any command not exercised by a test (e.g. `capture_report_document` once returned a `ReportDocument` instead of `DocumentCaptureResult`, caught only by a Playwright journey).

A stronger gate would type each handler's return against the command's ts-rs-generated return type (a typed command->returnType map, so a wrong-shaped return fails `tsc`). For now the convention is a documented rule in docs/testing.md ('Mock runtime conventions': return the contract shape, not the entity; extract via `callCommand<T>("cmd")`).

Scope: build a typed dispatch table mapping each command name to its generated return type and constrain the handler return to it. Non-trivial (156 commands, varied shapes) — hence tracked, not done inline.

body:

comments.body:
§A0 real-data spike findings (owner DB, mode=ro consistent copy, 2026-07-27)

COVERAGE
1a. 51 companies, ALL confirmed (10950 facts, 0 unconfirmed). Periods: FY=885, quarterly=58 (Q1=50,Q3=5,H1=3) -> annual is the only viable comparison axis; quarterly QoQ is near-empty. Revenue+net_profit FY depth: 49/51 have >=5 periods (max 23: LPP/MDV); only edge = CRQ (3 rev), DIA/SCW (5). Banks PEO/PKO: 0 revenue, 22/19 net_profit (report interest income, not revenue). Effectively ALL companies have >=2 periods for revenue/net_profit.
1b. sector: 51/51 populated (sector_source=registry). 34 distinct sectors. Histogram N=6(1),N=4(1),N=2(9),N=1(23). Only 2 sectors reach N>=4: oprogramowanie(6), Nowe Technologie(4) = 10 companies. -> 41/51 (80%) will be thin-flagged. Taxonomy also fragmented (software split across oprogramowanie/systemy informatyczne/Nowe Technologie).
1c. currency: PLN 98.5%, NULL 0.8% (83, genuine monetary gaps -> exercises currency_unknown flag), 'shares' 0.7% (76, all on eps_basic/eps_diluted -> MISLABEL: EPS is PLN/share not 'shares'). ZERO EUR/USD facts. FY range 2004-2026. Universe 100% PLN, 50 GPW + 1 NC.

GROUND TRUTH: private/realdata/v061-alignment-ground-truth.json - 3 pairs: ACP|COG revenue (deep 22yr), KGH|PKN net_profit (deep, signed/losses), CRQ|SCW revenue (SPARSE: union 2021-2025, CRQ gaps 2021&2025 typed no_fact). NBP sample: private/realdata/nbp-sample.json.

NBP PROBE: shape {table,code,rates:[{no,effectiveDate,mid}]}. History floor 2002-01-02 (pre-2002=404). Trading days only (weekends skipped -> helpers must tolerate gaps). Window limit 367 days, no pagination -> full backfill = ~24 chunks/currency.

TRIPWIRE VERDICTS
(i) peer depth <=2 meaningless? NOT triggered (max N=6). BUT caveat: only 10/51 companies non-thin; 41/51 thin. Percentiles/confidence-grade honest-but-mostly-thin as specced (ADR dec.3 N<4). No design change needed; expect thin state to be the norm.
(ii) NBP shallower than oldest non-PLN fact? NOT triggered - zero non-PLN facts exist; oldest FY=2004 > NBP floor 2002. FLAG: ADR 0089 dec.2 'real FX layer now' has NO live data to convert today (100% PLN); FX substrate is entirely forward-looking (US/EU adapters). Suggest: build it, but tests must synthesize non-PLN facts - real-data validation of conversion is impossible on current corpus.
(iii) currency NULL-heavy >30%? NOT triggered (0.8% NULL).

NO STOP-AND-ASK. Proceed to A1/A2. Two non-blocking flags for orchestrator: (a) eps currency='shares' mislabel (file bug); (b) FX has no real data -> synthetic test facts required.

title: ROIC/ROCE are uncomputable — synthetic intermediates unresolved; ADR 0046 overstates it
body: The v0.34 catalog seeds roic = nopat / invested_capital and roce = operating_profit / capital_employed, but nopat, invested_capital, and capital_employed are neither seeded reported metrics nor resolved anywhere — so the metrics service returns Unavailable ('No data') for these two headline quality metrics even with full facts. roe (net_profit / total_equity) works. ADR 0046 Decision 1 claims 'the small remainder are built-in resolvers documented alongside the engine', which is not implemented — a doc/code drift. Fix: either implement explicit resolvers (and document the financial conventions, e.g. effective tax rate for NOPAT — must not be silently guessed) or seed these as reported inputs / redefine the formulas over available metrics; then correct ADR 0046 to match. title: Study portalanaliz.pl as a source candidate
body:
Study whether portalanaliz.pl can be used as a reliable and legally acceptable Brawler source before any implementation.

Questions to answer:
- Do terms and conditions, robots policy, or copyright posture allow automated access, scraping, RSS/API use, caching, and redistribution of snippets/metadata inside an open-source desktop app?
- Is there an official RSS, API, sitemap, or other stable source path that avoids fragile scraping?
- What data would be useful for Brawler: company analysis, articles, tags, publication dates, source URLs, authors, tickers, or watchlist-relevant updates?
- Does the site provide enough stable company/ticker signal for safe matching?
- What attribution, rate-limit, caching, source enable/disable, and developer-diagnostics policy would be required?
- Could this become Brawler's first license-gated feature if the source is legally acceptable and valuable enough?

Product/licensing angle:
- Compare open-core optional source access versus a license-gated premium source integration.
- Assess whether gating source refresh, source availability, or advanced analysis is technically clean with the existing entitlement boundaries.
- Identify any source-terms, attribution, caching, or user-expectation concerns created by making this a paid/gated feature.

Acceptance criteria:
- Document source-policy conclusion: reject, keep as developer-only candidate, implement optional source, seek explicit permission, or candidate for license-gated premium source.
- Do not implement scraping unless a source-specific ADR approves it.
- If implementation is recommended, define adapter boundary, matching strategy, tests, user-facing attribution, and entitlement boundary before coding.

title: bug(ai-pool): TextOnly member in a Document-capability pool always hard-fails and poisons failover
body: S6 review (R2 #2, 2026-07-02): the build guard rejects only DocumentSupport::None, but kpi/claim extraction always sends AnalysisDocument::Native (kpi_extraction.rs:220) and a TextOnly provider (provider_openai, provider_openai_compatible) returns ProviderError on Native (openai.rs:258) — a NON-availability error. Consequences: (a) a TextOnly-only pool for kpi_extraction/claim_extraction passes validation+build but every extraction hard-fails; (b) in a mixed pool [gemini(Native), compatible(TextOnly)], during Gemini's 60s cooldown the warm TextOnly member is promoted first and short-circuits every document extraction (immediate return Err, no further failover). Fix direction: reject non-Native members for Document-kind capabilities at build/validation, OR treat document-kind-mismatch as skip-and-continue in the pool. Fold in R2 #7 (job metadata attributes the pool's members[0], not the actually-serving member), #8 (the 'no usable provider' error should enumerate per-member skip reasons), #9 (autopilot test-sample guard checks only the primary member — defense-in-depth).

title: Assess X.com as a source candidate
body:
Study whether X.com/Twitter can be a viable and legally acceptable source for Brawler before any implementation.

Questions to answer:
- Does X provide an official API tier that fits Brawler's local-first desktop use, cost posture, rate limits, and open-source distribution?
- Do X terms allow automated access, caching, indexing, display of posts, and source attribution inside a desktop app?
- Is scraping prohibited or too fragile to consider under Brawler's source policy?
- What source value would X provide: company announcements, executive posts, journalist/investor feeds, market rumors, or event detection?
- How would Brawler avoid low-quality/noisy or market-manipulative content, and how would source trust be labeled?
- What privacy, credential, API-key, and user-account requirements would this introduce?

Acceptance criteria:
- Document conclusion: reject, official-API-only candidate, developer-only candidate, or implement optional source.
- Do not implement scraping unless a source-specific ADR explicitly approves it.
- If viable, define source adapter boundary, trust labeling, rate-limit/cache policy, attribution rules, and tests before coding.

title: epic: Story clustering across sources
body:
Goal: collapse near-duplicate coverage of the same event from multiple sources (ESPI filing, Bankier article, RSS item) into one story so the feed reads as a briefing, not a firehose.

Scope:
- cluster model and similarity rules (URL/title normalization heuristics first; embedding similarity later if needed)
- canonical-source ranking inside a cluster (official filing outranks media coverage)
- clustering during ingestion with idempotent re-clustering
- clustered rendering in the feed/inbox with expandable members

Out of scope: cross-company clustering; sentiment or importance scoring.

Exit criteria: a real event covered by ESPI and Bankier renders as one story with the filing on top; cluster membership survives refreshes without duplicates.

comments.body: Outcome: EVALUATED AND DROPPED. Cross-source story clustering was implemented heuristic-first and validated against a real production DB (49 companies, 401 items, official komunikaty + media RSS). No local method reaches trustworthy precision at useful recall — best local result precision 0.79 / recall 0.73 (~1 in 5 merges wrong); lexical recall ~0.2-0.4; e5-small embeddings can't separate same-event (0.90) from unrelated (0.89). It is also a nice-to-have at real scale, not core. Implementation reverted (no released DB touched). The reliable path is an LLM judge, deferred to a future milestone behind the AI provider boundary. The v0.45.0 embedding model is re-pointed to semantic search (v0.48) + RAG retrieval (v0.47/0.49/0.50). Full rationale + evidence: ADR 0051. Closing the epic and its sub-issues as not-shipped.

title: Report-document backfill stores wrong attachment URL (title↔URL company mismatch)
body: Discovered during the v0.47.0 real-data spike (ADR 0052). In the maintainer's real DB, several CyberFolks (CBF) report_documents rows carry titles like 'cyber_Folks_2025_Q2_SSF.pdf' but their url points at a DIFFERENT company's attachment — e.g. bankier.pl .../Vercom-2025-Q1-SSF... and .../Raport-srodroczny-Grupy-Shoper-H1-2025... The app-assigned title says CBF while the stored URL (and therefore the bytes a fetch would pull) belong to Vercom/Shoper. This is a data-integrity bug in the backfill attachment resolution: the title and url are sourced/paired incorrectly. Impact: a fetched 'CBF' report would contain another issuer's data, corrupting KPI extraction, citations, and the new report diff. Repro: query report_documents for company_gpw_cbf where url LIKE '%bankier.pl%' and compare the URL filename's company token against the title. Affects the older bankier.pl-hosted rows; newer bonnier.pl rows are self-consistent.

title: epic: Local interpretative AI layer (on-device semantic lookup)
body:
Design: ADR 0035 (two-layer AI architecture). Extends ADR 0028 (generative provider boundary).

Goal: an always-on, on-device interpretative layer (embeddings + light classifiers) for fast, free, offline, private semantic lookup, behind capability contracts so models are replaceable/upgradeable and the whole layer is reversible to a static baseline.

Binding constraints (ADR 0035):
- Consumers bind to CAPABILITIES (Classifier, SimilarityProvider, Matcher, SemanticSearch), never to a model.
- Static/deterministic implementation is the shipped baseline; the model implementation is an optional enhancement behind the same interface (removal = switch active impl, no consumer change).
- Separate engine boundary (Embedder, model_id+dim) for swapping the model/runtime.
- Interpretative layer produces ONLY disposable derived/index data (vector store, sqlite-vec-class); removing the model drops a derived table with zero canonical data loss.
- Selection via registry + config (reuse ADR 0028 pattern); conservative static defaults, model opt-in.
- Per-capability eval harness decides keep/drop on data.

Proposed defaults (confirm via eval): pure-Rust inference (candle/fastembed), multilingual encoder evaluated on Polish (e5/bge class), sqlite-vec vector store, weights as optional download.

First consumers: Classifier (v0.39.0 ESPI), SimilarityProvider (v0.45.0 story clustering), Matcher/SemanticSearch (claims, hybrid search).

Out of scope: local generative LLM (future ADR 0028 adapter); speculative capabilities with no near-term caller.

UNSCHEDULED pending owner sequencing decision; embedding-model implementation may be split into a follow-on milestone.

comments.body: Closing with v0.52.0: the static half (rule classifier — live consumer: signal classification) was delivered in v0.39/v0.40 and stays; the embedding-model half (e5-small, vector store, similarity strategies) was delivered in v0.45 but no capability ever beat the static baseline in a per-capability eval (clustering dropped in ADR 0051, SemanticSearch never landed, report-diff shipped without similarity). ADR 0035's reversible-to-static safety valve was exercised in v0.52.0: model + vector scaffold retired (ADR 0080, R1, -57 crates, forward migrations 0069/0070). Epic outcome: partially delivered, remainder deliberately retired with evidence.

title: epic: 100% deterministic fundamentals data gathering (ADR 0061)
body:
Cross-cutting fundamentals-reliability epic (no milestone label), ADR 0061. Supersedes ADR 0060's Gemini-Pro-for-documents premise; amends ADR 0055/0036; relates to ADR 0052/0028/0027/0049.

Owner requirement: 100% deterministic, 100% automatic KPI gathering, no human-in-the-loop as steady state. Truth: provable determinism only from structured/tagged data, not raw PDF.

S0 coverage spike (owner DB, done): 264 xHTML/iXBRL + 6 XBRL docs already referenced but almost all unfetched; of companies with reports ~8 structured vs ~30 PDF-only. PDF text extraction reliable (ADR 0052); naive PL dictionary matched 15/17 core KPIs on real CBF 2026 Q1 (~90%). => multi-tier is right.

Layered pipeline (a KPI taken from highest tier; every fact validated or flagged, never silently wrong):
- Tier 1 ESEF/iXBRL (annual): parse ix:nonFraction + IFRS concept->metric_key. Fetch path must retrieve the already-discovered structured packages.
- Tier 2 structured xHTML 'wybrane dane' (some interims).
- Tier 3 deterministic PDF parser (PL label dictionary + column/unit/sign) + per-company versioned extraction profile + drift->learning loop.
- Tier 4 HTML aggregator (BiznesRadar/Bankier/StockWatch - NOT Stooq) as routine second witness + fallback.
- Last resort AI over extracted TEXT via provider pool.

'Good' gate = accounting identities + comparative-period cross-check + structure match + completeness. Per-company bootstrap once, then zero-touch + self-validating; drift -> notify with clean diff + re-learn.

AI provider pool (S6): ordered (provider,model) per capability, failover on 5xx/429/timeout + cooldown; builds on ADR 0059 gate + ADR 0060 routing; availability not correctness. Related epic e1c3fac (ADR 0060 provider routing) feeds S6.

Slices: S0 ADR+spike (done); S1 validation layer; S2 ESEF parser; S3 PDF parser+profiles; S4 HTML aggregator; S5 wire into autopilot + drift-notification UI + e2e pipeline test + clickable tests; S6 AI provider pool.

Guardrail (ADR 0045): no fact emitted without validation status; e2e pipeline test (sample bytes, run_until_idle) + real-data harness before default flip.

title: epic: Autonomous report pipeline
body:
Goal: close the loop so a tracked company's new periodic report is fetched, extracted, analyzed, and surfaced as a notified summary cross-referenced against existing claims, questions, and evidence — with no manual steps — once the user trusts extraction quality.

This is a capstone that composes existing building blocks: calendar/cockpit (v0.40) detects the publication, report document persistence (v0.34) fetches it, KPI extraction (v0.35) reads the numbers, report diff (v0.44) and digests (v0.31) summarize the change, and the claims tracker (v0.39) supplies the cross-references. The new ingredient is autonomous orchestration plus a trust ladder.

Trust ladder (accepted): confirm-before-commit stays the global default. The user may opt a specific company into auto-confirm. Auto-committed facts carry a distinct unreviewed provenance state so they remain visibly flagged, reversible, and fully cited. The global default is not flipped.

Scope:
- per-company autopilot setting and the auto/unreviewed provenance state
- publish detection from calendar/events for tracked companies
- auto-fetch + auto-extract chained on detection while the app is running
- auto-confirm path with a reversible review queue for unreviewed facts
- a composed result notification: summary, KPI deltas, report diff, and cross-references to claims/questions/evidence

Out of scope: fetching or analyzing while the app is closed (that is a hosted/scheduled service and belongs to the managed-AI paid frontier, not core); flipping the global confirmation default.

Exit criteria: with autopilot enabled for one company, a newly published real report is fetched, extracted, auto-confirmed as unreviewed, and surfaced as a single notification with summary and cross-references, all without manual steps; every auto-confirmed fact remains cited and reversible.

- fetch the IR page HTML, extract candidate links
- hand the AI the candidate list + event context; it returns the best-matching report URL
- ambiguous/low-confidence -> surface candidates for the user to pick
- no per-company scrapers

title: epic: Report document ingestion & history backfill
body:
Goal: persist the actual report files and remove the cold-start problem when tracking a company.

Scope (deferred from v0.34.0, retargeted to the active Bankier official-report path):
- Persist ESPI/EBI report attachments and user-supplied report URLs as stored report documents with durable attribution, linked to feed item/evidence (task c178e8f).
- On-track / company-workspace action that backfills the last 2-3 years of periodic reports, recent filings, and calendar entries; backfilled items flow through normal ingestion with original publication dates preserved; idempotent re-runs (task cc72965).

Out of scope: per-company PDF parsers; deterministic ESEF/iXBRL parsing (separate study); backfilling non-official media; automatic backfill without user action.

Exit criteria: a real ESPI periodic report attachment and a user-supplied URL both persist as report documents with attribution and appear linked from company evidence; tracking a real GPW company yields a populated multi-year timeline with stored report documents; re-running produces no duplicates.

Split out of v0.39.0 (typed ESPI classification) because this depends on the Bankier article/attachment fetch path and live verification rather than on classification.

title: Derive per-company KPI relevance profile from reports
body:
Goal: have the agent determine which KPIs (standard and non-standard) actually matter for a given company by reading its report, instead of applying a fixed template — so a pre-revenue company is not judged on revenue.

Scope:
- extract the company's self-declared KPIs from 'Selected KPIs' sections, management commentary, and segment tables
- combine with the sector default pack to propose a ranked relevance profile (primary/secondary)
- propose new custom KPI definitions discovered in the report (e.g. GMV, profit-per-lot, backlog), not only values for known KPIs
- user curates the profile (confirm/add/drop/reorder) and confirms new definitions before they persist; proposals follow the same confirmation rule as extracted facts

Out of scope: cross-company KPI vocabulary sharing; automatic profile changes without user confirmation.

Exit criteria: for a real report (e.g. cyber_Folks), the agent proposes a relevance profile whose primary KPIs match what management foregrounds, including at least one non-standard KPI as a new custom definition, all behind user confirmation.

title: Plan reusable dense row primitive
body:

Decision:
- Add a reusable DenseRow shell under src/ui for shared selected, unread, disabled, hover, and focus state behavior.
- Keep row body layout screen-owned for now because current row families differ materially: feed/evidence rows, entity rows, source/transcript rows, event rows, and form-like settings/shortcut rows.
- Migrate compatible row families incrementally instead of forcing a universal row component.

Migration order:
1. Source and transcript rows, because they already share source-row structure.
2. Feed and research evidence rows, because they share selection/action behavior but need source-specific body metadata.
3. Entity rows such as companies and watchlists after the shell proves stable.
4. Event rows remain separate unless later evidence shows enough overlap.

Acceptance criteria:
- Identify row families that can share a primitive without hiding domain differences.
- Decide the row API shape and migration order.
- Do not force a generic row if screen-specific behavior remains too different.

title: flaky: SettingsScreen 'persists theme changes' vitest times out (5033/5000ms) under full-gate load
body:
Observed 2026-07-08 blocking a pre-commit run of make check: src/screens/Settings/SettingsScreen.test.tsx 'shows local settings and persists theme changes' timed out at 5033ms vs the 5000ms default budget. Passes in isolation in ~2.7s of test time. The full-suite run showed heavy contention (transform 44s, import 93s across workers).

Class: load-sensitive vitest tests sitting at the edge of the default timeout make the mandatory gate nondeterministic — an agent hitting this rightly stops, wasting a full gate cycle.

Fix direction (deliberate, not a blind bump): either give this workflow test an explicit generous timeout with a comment, or reduce its userEvent round-trips; consider a lint/guard for workflow tests within 20% of the default budget under nominal timing. Do NOT weaken the gate itself.

comments.body: Second occurrence, same gate cycle, different test: TodayScreen 'prioritized attention stream' assertion missed the 'verify' category under full-suite load (2 failed / 533 passed), while SettingsScreen timed out again (5149ms). Both pass in isolation (23/23, ~6s). Class confirmed: full-gate vitest parallelism makes edge tests nondeterministic — one flake blocked the same pre-commit twice in a row. Raising practical priority: this directly burns gate cycles.

title: epic: UX quality loop v2 — experience contracts, adversarial validation, continuous dogfooding
body:
Goal: make Brawler validate UX decisions as deliberately as it validates code behavior, reducing frontend and UX defects that pass a green TDD gate.

Context:
- ADR 0074 delivered journey specs, clickable E2E, and interaction budgets.
- ADR 0076 delivered design tokens, density contracts, accessibility checks, and visual baselines.
- Escaped defects still cluster in specification gaps, visual hierarchy, discoverability, async transitions, real-content shapes, and late owner validation.
- Existing epic 0db7a7a owns the generic failure-path, chaos-mode, poor-state, and real-DB test foundation. This epic consumes that foundation for UX validation and must not create a second mock runtime.

Outcome:
1. Every non-mechanical UI feature starts from an approved experience contract: user trigger, desired outcome, information hierarchy, primary action, storyboard, and state matrix.
2. Journey validation measures navigation and cognitive friction in addition to raw interaction count.
3. Frontend scenarios cover hostile content, partial failure, stale processing, dense history, and controlled async ordering.
4. Visual review produces a compact contact sheet across relevant states, pane sizes, and themes.
5. Real-app exploratory validation happens after the first vertical slice and mid-milestone, not only at release closure.
6. Escaped UX defects are classified and trended so the process fixes planning gaps instead of reflexively adding tests.
7. A J1/J2 pilot demonstrates fewer integration surprises and produces the final reusable contract.

Non-goals:
- replacing make check, ADR 0074 journeys, ADR 0076 visual baselines, or owner judgment;
- adding screenshot tests for every transient state;
- weakening deterministic gates or adding global retries;
- duplicating the failure-path infrastructure in 0db7a7a;
- redesigning product screens without their own approved feature scope.

Delivery posture:
- Cross-cutting process and test-architecture epic; no product milestone label.
- Canonical docs and a durable ADR amendment land before enforcement.
- Roll out through a J1 morning-review and J2 report-published pilot before making the new DoD universal.

Epic definition of done:
- all child contracts and tooling are delivered and documented;
- the J1/J2 pilot runs against browser scenarios and the real Windows app;
- make check remains deterministic and within the existing low-minutes budget;
- the retrospective records which escaped-defect classes were caught earlier and which remain human-only;
- owner signs off before the epic is marked solved.

title: Release: add prepare/curate/finalize split so curated changelog lands in the tagged commit
body: make release runs in one shot: bump -> make changelog (terse scaffold) -> checks -> commit -> tag -> push, with no pause to curate. So the tagged CHANGELOG (which the GitHub release notes are sliced from) is always terse, forcing a post-hoc gh release edit AND a second master CHANGELOG commit — the latter being the source of repeated 'unasked follow-up commit' friction. Proposal: add make release-prepare VERSION=x (bump + changelog scaffold, then stop for curation), and change make release's abort-guards (already-bumped / changelog-section-exists) into skip-if-already-done so it finalizes a prepared release into a single curated chore(release) commit. title: epic: UI coherence — adopt and extend the shared component framework
body:
Goal: make views coherent by adopting the existing src/ui primitives everywhere and extracting the few shapes still reinvented per screen. Inline styles are not the issue (1 in the whole codebase); the issue is screens hand-rolling equivalents of primitives that already exist.

Evidence (measured):
- SectionHeader used in only 4 places, but ~20 distinct ad-hoc header/toolbar classes do the same job (section-heading x6, feed-panel x6, notebook-entry-header x5, diagnostics-section-header x5, notebook-toolbar, fact-detail-header, watchlist-detail-header, ...).
- TextField/SelectField adopted in only 6 files; 10+ screens use raw <select> and several use many raw <input> (FundamentalsPanel 6, CompanyWorkspace 4, CompaniesScreen 4). No TextareaField, so note/claim bodies are raw <textarea>.
- Two competing badges: StatusPill (13) vs StatusChip (5), no rule for which to use.
- error-text hand-rolled in ~15 files; no ErrorText primitive.
- Media rows (icon + truncating title + trailing meta/badge/action) reinvented in report-docs, feed attachments, source rows. DetailSection already bakes the min-width:0 containment some panels hand-roll.

Workstreams (tasks): section headers; form controls; status-badge unification; new primitives (ListRow/ErrorText/Hint); governance (lint + docs + visual tests). All judged equally important by owner.

Constraint (modularization-design.md): do not mass-convert markup during feature work; this is a deliberate coherence pass. Preserve class semantics and accessibility; some natives (segmented controls, row selectors, anchor links) may stay by design.

Not yet milestone-scheduled. A pilot retrofit of the v0.41 report-document + backfill panels lands first to prove the approach.

comments.body:
Reprioritization (owner): the PRIMARY deliverable of this epic is closing the agent-guidance system gap, not the retrofits. Root cause: agents hand-roll UI because the component guidance is (a) not discoverable where agents look, (b) not explicit enough, (c) not enforced. Retrofits are necessary but secondary — without the guidance fix, incoherence regenerates on the next feature.

System fix has three layers, all required:
1. Discoverability — a prominent pointer in AGENTS.md Required Reading: 'before writing/editing any frontend UI, read the UI authoring guide and use src/ui primitives; never hand-roll controls/sections/badges.' Today AGENTS.md points only to ui-flows / ui-information-architecture (UX), not a component-authoring guide.
2. Explicitness — a canonical UI authoring guide: the primitive catalog, a 'do not hand-roll X -> use Y' table, the canonical badge, form-control/section-header/list-row/error/hint rules, and a pre-write self-check ('does a src/ui primitive already do this? check ui/index.ts'). Plus an ADR recording the primitive-first + enforcement policy.
3. Enforcement — an ESLint rule failing CI on raw <input>/<select>/style={{ outside src/ui/, so violations are caught mechanically, not left to memory.

Task 40e805d is elevated to the lead task and priority:high. The pilot will seed layers 1-2 (guide + AGENTS pointer) immediately as the proof.

title: Inbox shows 0 items on 'Wszystko' while feed_items has current rows (live app)
body: Seen on the owner's live app during the F4 drive (2026-07-10, v0.50.0 uncommitted branch build): Inbox with status filter 'Wszystko', all watchlists, no search shows 'Brak elementow kanalu dla wybranych filtrow' and 0/0/0 counters, while the DB has July 2026 feed_items (they render in the cockpit Kanal pane). Either a filter/read-model regression or a legitimate-but-misleading default; needs a repro against the read model. Found incidentally - not diagnosed further during F4 QG.

comments.body: Root cause found (not a read-model bug): live DB has 728 feed_items, 372 matching the list_feed_items predicate — the backend returns rows. The Inbox list is feedState filtered client-side; six cross-navigation flows each hand-rolled a DIFFERENT partial filter reset (global-search feed_item nav and research-evidence 'feed' nav forgot the signal filter; research 'ai_analysis' nav and company-scoped flows set ONLY the company filter, leaving status/type/source/watchlist/search stale). title: Autopilot detection ranks reports by created_at, not report date — fires on stale reports after backfill
body: Discovered during 7b08af8 real-data validation (private/realdata, company_gpw_cbf). newest_periodic_reports_per_type (src-tauri/src/jobs/autopilot.rs) keeps the doc with the greatest created_at per statement type. created_at is the LOCAL ingestion timestamp, not the report's publication/period date. After a ~3-year history backfill, old reports get a newer created_at than recent ones, so detection selects a stale report as 'newest'. Real-data evidence: cbf 2023 Q2 SSF/JSF created_at=2026-06-15T16:49:36.268Z vs 2026 Q1 SSF created_at=...167Z (all backfilled same second) -> detection started autopilot runs on the 2023 Q2 reports, not 2026 Q1. This breaks the v0.49 promise (fire on a newly published report). Fix: rank by the report's actual publication/period date (period end via period_id, or a parsed filing date), not created_at; add a real-data-shaped test. Repro: run autopilot_real_data_validation against private/realdata with BRAWLER_REAL_COMPANY=company_gpw_cbf.

Guarded by test newest_per_type_ranks_by_disclosure_not_created_at (autopilot.rs:1490-1511), which fixtures a 2023 report given a newer created_at than a 2026 report's older created_at and asserts the 2026 (correct domain-date) report wins — exactly the backfill scenario from this issue. cargo nextest run autopilot: 23 passed (src-tauri); targeted rerun of this test alone: 1 passed. title: ACP: pozycja 'kapitał własny (jednostki dominującej)' mapowana na total_equity/total → fałszywy konflikt slotu (attribution owners_of_parent nigdy nie emitowany)
body:
## Objaw (owner dogfooding, żywa apka, 2026-07-12)
Kokpit GPW:ACP → panel "Do przeglądu". Propozycja OCR dla slotu
**"kapitał własny (przypisany akcjonariuszom jednostki dominującej)" = 7,43 mld**
(2026 Q1) czerwieni się komunikatem konfliktu: "dla tego slotu zapisano już
inną wartość (zapisano 13 484 800 000,0, ta propozycja 7 425 700 000,0)".

## Przyczyna źródłowa
To są **dwie różne pozycje bilansu**, nie konflikt:
- **13,48 mld** = *Total equity* (attribution=`total`, ze strukturalnej ścieżki
  `api`/ESEF) — pełny kapitał skonsolidowany **łącznie z udziałami
  niekontrolującymi**. Poprawne. Asseco ma ogromne mniejszości (Formula Systems
  itd.), więc różnica z pozycją "jednostki dominującej" jest duża i realna.
- **7,43 mld** = *equity attributable to owners of the parent* — propozycja OCR
  poprawnie odczytała liczbę, ale **zmapowała ją na `metric_key=total_equity`
  z `attribution=total`** (domyślne), więc wpadła w ten sam slot co total equity.

Slot to `(period_id, definition_id, statement_basis, attribution, variant,
measure_window, data_quality)`. Data-model **już definiuje**
`attribution ∈ {total, owners_of_parent, nci}` (data-model.md:625), więc pozycja
"przypisany akcjonariuszom jednostki dominującej" powinna trafić do slotu
`attribution=owners_of_parent` — inny slot, **zero konfliktu**.

Weryfikacja na żywej bazie: `select distinct attribution from financial_facts`
zwraca **tylko `total`** — wymiar `owners_of_parent`/`nci` jest w specyfikacji,
ale **żadna ścieżka ekstrakcji go nie emituje**. Ekstraktor (OCR/PDF; podejrzenie
też AI i strukturalna) dopasowuje synonim "kapitał własny" i **ignoruje
kwalifikator** "(przypisany akcjonariuszom jednostki dominującej)".

## Guard zadziałał poprawnie
Komunikat konfliktu = bezpieczne zachowanie (ADR 0077 `value_conflict`: nie
nadpisuje, oddaje decyzję userowi). Problem nie w guardzie, lecz w tym, że user
jest proszony o pogodzenie dwóch wartości, które **nie powinny być w tym samym
slocie**.

## Obejście teraz (dla ownera)
**Odrzuć** tę propozycję — zapisana wartość 13,48 mld (total equity) jest
poprawna. Odrzucenie niczego nie psuje.

## Zakres naprawy (do decyzji)
1. Detekcja kwalifikatora attribution w taksonomii ekstrakcji: "przypisany
   akcjonariuszom jednostki dominującej" / "attributable to owners of the
   parent" → `attribution=owners_of_parent`; "udziały niekontrolujące" /
   "non-controlling interests" → `attribution=nci`. PL+EN, warianty odmiany.
2. Zastosować spójnie na wszystkich ścieżkach (strukturalna ESEF już filtruje
   dimensional NCI-component z total — sprawdzić, czy przy okazji nie gubi
   pozycji owners_of_parent; OCR/PDF; AI).
3. Rozważyć, czy panel jakości/coverage ma pokazywać rozbicie
   total / owners_of_parent / NCI (wartość dla inwestora: mniejszości ważą przy
   ROE per-akcjonariusz).
4. Test na realnym raporcie Asseco (klasyczny przypadek dużych mniejszości) jako
   ground-truth.

Powiązania: ADR 0061 (deterministyczna ekstrakcja), ADR 0077 (trusted
extraction, `value_conflict`), data-model.md §financial_facts (attribution).

title: epic: Report-over-report diff
body:
Goal: show what actually changed between consecutive periodic reports — section-level text comparison plus an AI-summarized delta with citations into both documents — so the investor stops rereading 80 unchanged pages.

Scope:
- text extraction and section alignment for stored report documents
- deterministic section-level diff between consecutive filings of the same type
- AI delta summary (new risks, changed segment commentary, tone shifts) with citations into both documents and full provenance
- diff view reachable from the company workspace and on new report arrival

Out of scope: diffing across different companies; financial table reconciliation (owned by KPI extraction).

Exit criteria: two consecutive real quarterly reports produce a navigable diff and a cited delta summary; closure demoed against a real GPW company.

comments.body:
Planning + real-data spike complete → ADR 0052. SCOPE NARROWED to structured financial statements (consolidated SSF / standalone JSF), pure-Rust deterministic diff, no AI this milestone.

Real-data evidence (11 PDFs, 6 issuers): pure-Rust pdf-extract is reliable across formats (alpha-ratio 0.80-0.89, Polish diacritics intact, incl. signed + deflate-encoded). Structured statements align 85-92% by heading with a deterministic self-diff = empty invariant; the narrative management report (MD&A) aligns only 4% by heading. Therefore MD&A diff + AI delta summary are DEFERRED to a later milestone (needs stronger section detection + embedding-backed alignment).

Decisions: (1) deterministic Rust extraction, AI only deferred; (2) heading+lexical alignment with positional consumption, embedding model as optional enhancer (never a hard dependency); (3) persist derived report_document_sections, diff is an on-demand read model. Docs updated: ADR 0052, data-model, contracts, product-spec, ui-flows, ui-IA, roadmap, testing.

title: Extend data model for financial periods, facts, and KPI definitions
body:
Goal: add the fundamentals entities to docs/data-model.md and a migration, per ADR 0027 (validated against ~37 GPW companies). KPI side is a three-layer model (catalog / relevance / facts) so it stays flexible across sectors.

Tables:
- company adds statement_type (industrial/bank/insurer/specialty-finance) selecting which canonical packs apply, plus a fiscal_year_end offset (non-calendar years: Text Apr-Mar, LPP Feb-Jan, Synektik offset)
- financial_periods: company, fiscal year, granularity (monthly/quarter/H1/9M/FY), report evidence ref; discrete vs YTD handled via fact measure_window
- kpi_definitions (catalog): key, label, value_kind (monetary/percentage/ratio/count/physical), unit (typed: PLN/EUR/USD, t, t/day, m2, count, per-unit), display format, computation (reported|derived with formula over keys), and scope (canonical/sector/company); seed packs: universal, industrial, cash-flow, capital-efficiency (derived), insurance, banking, specialty-finance; custom defaults to company scope, promotable
- kpi_relevance (selection, temporal): company x definition link with status (active/archived), source (user/agent/sector), first_seen/last_seen, rank
- financial_facts (values): reference a definition; decimal-exact value (TEXT + rust_decimal) in base units, signed allowed, as-reported form/scale in provenance; dimensions: currency (per fact), statement_basis (consolidated/standalone), attribution (total/owners-of-parent/NCI), variant (reported/adjusted/constant-currency/continuing/discontinued/net-of-cancellations), measure_window (flow/point_in_time/trailing/cumulative), data_quality (final/estimated) with supersession link (final supersedes estimate, estimate history kept), extraction_method, confidence, confirmation_state (extensible to auto-unreviewed for autopilot), source document ref

Notes: derived metrics (FCF, ROE, ROIC, net_debt_to_ebitda) computed at read time incl. TTM; segment-specific KPIs (RevPAR, DOOH screens) represented as custom KPIs in v1 (segment dimension deferred); a fact may exist for a KPI not yet in the active profile; migration registered in storage/migrations.rs.

Exit criteria: data-model doc section merged; migration applies cleanly on existing databases; packs seeded; entity rules cover the three-layer separation, all fact dimensions, supersession, and statement types.

title: Study EODHD as a fundamentals verification and backfill source
body:
Goal: determine whether the EODHD API can legally, reliably, and affordably improve the fundamentals workflow before adding it to source implementation scope.

Positioning under review: bootstrap and verification only, never primary truth — report-extracted facts outrank API facts when both exist; API-sourced facts carry visibly lighter provenance (API attribution and retrieval date, no source document).

Questions:
- GPW/NewConnect coverage quality: how complete, correct, and timely are fundamentals for the small and mid caps actually tracked, not just WIG20? Test against real tracked companies.
- Licensing: do EODHD terms permit storing fetched data locally and long-term in a personal local-first desktop app with a user-supplied key?
- Cost-to-value: is the fundamentals tier price justifiable for individual users under the BYO-key model, and what does the free tier allow for evaluation?
- Adjacent value: earnings calendar dates (report-season cockpit), insider transactions and corporate actions (ESPI classification cross-check), dividends — which are worth ingesting?
- Scope discipline: EODHD is primarily a price API and price data remains out of scope; the study must reaffirm that boundary or consciously move it via ADR.

Decision criteria:
- Do not implement unless usage terms permit local-first storage with user-supplied keys.
- Prefer integration as financial-fact cross-check (extraction vs API agreement signal in the confirmation UI) and on-track backfill, behind the standard source adapter and credential boundaries.
- Requires the financial facts schema (v0.34.0) and extraction pipeline (v0.35.0) to be live before any integration milestone is planned.
- If the study recommends implementation, record the source policy and adapter design in Source Strategy or a source-specific ADR before coding.

title: bug(jobs): enqueue_stage silently no-ops when a recreated run's deterministic job IDs already exist — runs stick at pending/fetch forever
body: Real root cause of the stuck CBF runs (found 2026-07-03 by real-data validation forensics): job IDs are deterministic (autopilot:{run_id}:{stage}, run_id deterministic on company+document). create_run_if_absent recreates a failed run, enqueue_first_stage -> jobs().enqueue() = INSERT OR IGNORE — if the job row already exists from a prior life (e.g. succeeded 2026-07-01), the insert is a silent no-op (Ok(false) never inspected, nothing logged) and the fresh run row is never picked up: permanently pending/fetch with no recovery. storage/jobs.rs already has reschedule() (resets a terminal row to pending) — enqueue_stage uses the wrong primitive for the re-arm case. Fix direction: on run (re)creation, enqueue_stage must reschedule existing terminal job rows (or inspect the not-inserted case and reschedule), with a test: run recreated over pre-existing succeeded jobs reaches a terminal state. Breaks the 5a8b752 self-heal in production; the fetch stage never even reaches the signal_dates panic fixed today.

comments.body: Fixed 2026-07-03. Root fix: enqueue_stage and detection-sweep re-arm now use reschedule() (re-arms terminal rows, never clobbers a running row, logs the not-armed case). Class sweep fixed two more instances of the same silent-no-op class: per-job retry (retry_kpi/claim/ai) and the startup content-embedding refresh (dead after first success). Guardrail: rule added to data-model.md Durable Job Queue Rules; 3 red-before/green-after tests incl. the exact real-DB stuck shape. Real-data validation on the production DB copy now PASSES: all 3 CBF runs reach succeeded/notify (20 KPIs auto-confirmed via structured extraction on the 2023 PDF). Full make check green (MAKE_CHECK_EXIT=0). Known non-scope: trigger_autopilot_run returns autopilot_run_in_progress on a stuck run (no re-arm) — irrelevant today (command has no UI caller, tracked in 7062f7e run-now scope).

title: Fact divergences on re-extraction: CDR 7 slots disagree with stored confirmed values (extraction vintage)
body: Surfaced by the v0.57 T3b health-facts backfill (2026-07-17): force re-extraction of CDR's stored ESEF packages produced 7 Divergent slot outcomes - the deterministic parser's current output disagrees with confirmed facts stored by an earlier extraction vintage. Values were NOT overwritten (slot model surfaced them). Needs a ratification pass: review each divergence (old vs new vs source document), decide which is right, and harvest the class (parser-vintage change detection? divergence review queue surface?). Unrelated to the F5 basis swap. Evidence: T3b run log + plan v0.57 T3 record.

comments.body:
## Adjudication (2026-07-18) — root cause: one scale-detection bug

Reproduced the v0.57 health-facts backfill over a throwaway copy of the live DB
(`private/realdata` idiom, `BRAWLER_REAL_DB`/`BRAWLER_REAL_DATA_DIR`). All 7
`Divergent` slots trace to a **single** deterministic-parser bug, not 7 issues.

### The 7 surfaced divergences (verdict: stored-correct, re-extraction WRONG)

All are CDR **2023 Q3** (consolidated/reported/final), stored `html_positional`.
Stored value came from the **English** condensed interim statement (correct);
the divergent re-extraction came from the **Polish** `Skonsolidowane sprawozdanie`
for the same period.

| # | metric | period | stored (correct) | re-extracted (wrong) | document says | verdict |
|---|--------|--------|------------------|----------------------|---------------|---------|
| 1 | operating_cash_flow | 2023 Q3 | 244 768 000 | 244 768 000 000 | "244 768" in thousands | stored-correct |
| 2 | investing_cash_flow | 2023 Q3 | -183 968 000 | -183 968 000 000 | "(183 968)" in thousands | stored-correct |
| 3 | financing_cash_flow | 2023 Q3 | -102 395 000 | -102 395 000 000 | "102 395" in thousands | stored-correct |
| 4 | total_assets | 2023 Q3 | 2 412 731 000 | 2 412 731 000 000 | "2 412 731" in thousands | stored-correct |
| 5 | total_equity | 2023 Q3 | 2 208 144 000 | 2 208 144 000 000 | "2 208 144" in thousands | stored-correct |
| 6 | revenue | 2023 Q3 | 767 692 000 | 767 692 000 000 | "767 692" in thousands | stored-correct |
| 7 | cash | 2023 Q3 | 236 232 000 | 236 232 000 000 | "236 232" in thousands | stored-correct |

**Root cause.** The Polish statement declares its scale "wszystkie kwoty … w tys.
zł" (in thousands, 106×) but its notes mention two millions amounts in NARRATIVE
prose ("około 95 mln zł", "co najmniej 16 mln zł"). `pdf::detect_unit_scale`
triggered `Millions` on the bare `mln zł` substring, over-scaling every figure
×1000. The English statement has no such token, so its stored values are correct.

### 2 further facts the fix EXPOSED (verdict: stored WRONG, re-extraction correct)

The same bug had already **created** two mis-scaled `auto_unreviewed` facts from
the Polish doc (no prior value existed, so no divergence was flagged — they landed
silently wrong):

| metric | period | stored (×1000 too big) | correct | document says |
|--------|--------|------------------------|---------|---------------|
| current_assets | 2023 Q3 | 1 137 807 000 000 | 1 137 807 000 | "1 137 807" in thousands |
| current_liabilities | 2023 Q3 | 164 335 000 000 | 164 335 000 | "164 335" in thousands |

Blast radius across the whole DB is exactly these 2 facts (all-company re-run: 0
other divergences).

### Fix (class-based, red-first)

1. **Parser (root cause).** `detect_unit_scale`: a millions *declaration*
   (`w mln`/`w milionach`) is authoritative; a bare `mln zł` token only implies
   millions when no thousands declaration is present. Red-first golden
   `prose_millions_token_does_not_override_a_thousands_declaration`.
2. **Data repair.** Forward, idempotent, self-healing migration **0099** corrects
   the two already-persisted facts ÷1000 (exact-value + source-doc + period +
   metric guards; only auto_unreviewed machine values, never a user-confirmed one).
   Never a direct DB write. Test
   `migration_0099_repairs_only_the_misscaled_cdr_q3_2023_facts`.
3. **Verified end-to-end:** after fix + 0099, the backfill produces **0
   divergences** across all companies; the two facts read 1 137 807 000 /
   164 335 000.

No runtime `Divergent`→correction-queue feature was built: every divergence here
is one parser bug, and the only stored-wrong data (2 auto_unreviewed facts) is
repaired by migration. The existing `Divergent` path already never overwrites.
Doc: `docs/data-model.md` (financial_facts provenance → unit-scale precedence).

title: 19 report documents are XML/ZIP/HTML mislabeled as .pdf — magic-byte routing may ADD coverage
body: Found by the v0.59 OCR evaluation spike (2026-07-21) and independently confirmed by the orchestrator on a random n=60 sample (2 of 60 = 3.3%, consistent with the spike's 19/430 = 4.4%). Files stored under a .pdf name are actually XML, ZIP, or HTML. They fail 100% today, for reasons that have nothing to do with OCR or parser quality — the pipeline routes on the extension and hands a non-PDF to the PDF reader. Spanning 7 companies. Several of the XML files look like STRUCTURED financial data, so routing on magic bytes rather than filename could ADD coverage (a structured tier could read them) rather than merely removing errors. Scope: detect the real container by magic bytes at fetch/extract time, route accordingly (XBRL/iXBRL/xHTML tiers already exist), and record a typed reason when the container is unsupported. Cheap relative to the payoff. Related: ADR 0061 tier routing, card fc692da (period derivation), the A4 harness for before/after measurement.

title: AV4 follow-up: fine-grained re-render scoping for screen contexts

title: Test foundation 1 (keystone): canonical sample-data factory + stateful per-test-isolated mock runtime
body:
KEYSTONE — blocking; unlocks both broad clickable coverage and safe parallelism. Design: ADR 0048 decisions 1-2.

Scope:
- Build a canonical, deterministic sample-data factory with named scenarios (empty, minimal, rich; per-area as needed). Fixed IDs/timestamps, no random/wall-clock. Materialized fresh per test.
- Rust seed builder over a fresh open_in_memory_database; project the same dataset shape into the browser mock runtime initial state.
- Make src/test/browserSmokeRuntime.ts STATEFUL and per-test isolated: create/update/delete handlers write into per-test state and reflect into subsequent reads; reset/clone per test; switch default keeps throwing for unhandled commands.
- NOT a checked-in mutable golden .sqlite (rejected — drifts vs migrations, breaks isolation).

DoD: a clickable create→assert→delete journey works against the mock runtime; Rust + browser layers share one dataset source of truth; per-test isolation verified (no cross-test bleed).

comments.body:
Keystone status: the functional goal (a STATEFUL, per-test-isolated mock runtime) is DELIVERED and verified in both layers — browserSmokeRuntime.ts (Playwright; create/rename/delete/membership/notebooks/companies/sources/settings all reflect into reads) and workflowHarness/ (Vitest; already stateful). Per-test isolation holds (fresh page per Playwright context; resetAppTestState per Vitest test). Verified by 5 clickable CRUD journeys + Watchlists state tests, all green.

Remaining B/C = unify the two mock layers into one shared canonical factory + a Rust seed builder. DECISION: defer this as a deliberate, separately-verified refactor rather than rushing it. Rationale: (1) both layers already meet the keystone's actual goal (stateful + isolated); (2) they target different runtimes (jsdom vs Chromium) and a big-bang unification touches ~298 frontend tests + the browser suite — high risk to the currently 100%-green state; (3) an unused Rust seed builder would be dead code (clippy/knip). This is the 'verify before handover, don't rush risky refactors' posture (AGENTS.md). Unification remains valuable for drift-prevention but is not urgent and should be its own slice.

title: epic: Multi-provider AI (Claude + OpenAI, BYO key)
body:
Add Anthropic (Claude) and OpenAI (ChatGPT) as AI providers alongside the existing Gemini provider, all free with a user-supplied API key, before the AI KPI extraction milestone builds on the provider boundary.

Rationale:
- AI KPI extraction (now v0.36.0) is the most AI-intensive feature on the roadmap; its hardest piece is delivering report documents (PDF/ESEF) to the model. Document/PDF input differs most across providers (Gemini inline_data vs Claude document blocks vs OpenAI). Designing that abstraction against >=2 providers now avoids baking in Gemini-shaped assumptions and retrofitting later.
- Claude is the strongest of the three at structured extraction from documents, directly lifting the v0.36 core loop.
- The owner already uses Claude and ChatGPT with their own keys (dogfooding).

Boundary assessment (verified in code):
- The AiAnalysisProvider trait (providers/analysis/types.rs) is genuinely neutral; request/response/error types are provider-agnostic; credentials use a generic keychain-backed CredentialDescriptor. No trait redesign needed.
- Coupling is at the wiring layer only: hardcoded match-dispatch on provider_id duplicated across jobs/ai_analysis.rs, jobs/research_briefs.rs, jobs/research_digests.rs, jobs/transcript_runner.rs; settings/import allowlists pinned to provider_gemini and gemini-only model lists; per-provider credential helpers called directly.
- Document/PDF input does not exist yet (GeminiAnalysisPart is text-only). Net-new design, best done multi-provider.

Scope:
- Registry/factory for provider resolution; Claude + OpenAI analysis adapters implementing AiAnalysisProvider; generalized settings + per-provider credentials + selection UI; document-input part abstraction on the trait with Gemini retrofitted; ADR update; tests + contracts.

Out of scope:
- Managed/hosted AI (a future paid tier); KPI extraction itself (v0.36.0); transcript-provider multi-provider beyond what the registry naturally enables.

Exit criteria:
- A user can select Gemini, Claude, or OpenAI, store each key in the OS keychain, and run existing AI analysis/brief/digest flows against any of them.
- Provider dispatch goes through one registry, not duplicated match arms.
- The trait can carry a document input part; Gemini implements it. All checks green; contracts/docs updated.

title: ADR 0061 dec. 4d completeness gate is inert in production — kpi_relevance is empty

title: Period derivation is the biggest fundamentals coverage gap — 83 periodic_ssf documents never reach extraction
body: Measured by the v0.59 A4 real-data harness (2026-07-21, owner DB copy, 400-document sample): 1144 of 1544 eligible stored documents never reach extraction at all because no reporting period can be derived from title/URL. Governance and auditor documents legitimately have no period, BUT 83 periodic_ssf documents (31.7% of that kind) are REAL FINANCIAL STATEMENTS invisible to the pipeline purely for want of a period parse. Real DB has 534 periodic_ssf documents total, so the absolute number is larger than the sample suggests. This is upstream of every tier: no parser improvement, new tier, or OCR can help a document extraction never attempts. Verdict from the harness author and confirmed by the orchestrator: this is a LARGER and CHEAPER coverage win than any new extraction tier. Scope: widen deterministic period derivation (title patterns, URL patterns, document metadata, the filing's own cover data), measured by re-running the A4 harness before/after. title: Move source-refresh scheduling to a Rust-side scheduler
body:
Follow-up from the v0.38.0 idle-refresh study (issue 28d6409). Source refresh is currently scheduled in the frontend via window.setInterval/setTimeout (src/app/useAppLifecycleEffects.ts), which is subject to webview background timer throttling and process suspension when the window is hidden/minimized.

For the current minute-scale cadence this is acceptable, but a Rust-side scheduler is more resilient to webview throttling and centralizes timing for the autonomous report pipeline (v0.47.0).

Scope: move the refresh/cleanup scheduling loop to the Rust side (Tauri async runtime), keep the poll-interval setting, jitter, and failure backoff; expose next-refresh state to the UI; preserve the app-open-only boundary (no background/closed fetching). See docs/architecture.md 'Source Refresh Scheduling'.
